title: Senate ethics body to tackle Bato’s ‘unsigned’ response
summary: The Senate ethics committee will tackle Sen. Ronald dela Rosa’s unsigned response to the complaint against him for his absences, according to committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore…

blocks.text: Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa attends the Senate session on Monday, May 11, 2026, hours before being placed under Senate protective custody amid reports of an alleged ICC arrest warrant.

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate ethics committee will tackle Sen. Ronald dela Rosa’s unsigned response to the complaint against him for his absences, according to committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III.

Dela Rosa has asked the Senate body to “hold the complaint in abeyance,” pending his petition before the Supreme Court against the enforcement of the arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity.
Sotto yesterday said his office received on Saturday Dela Rosa’s answer to the ethics complaint filed by the group “Wag Kang KuCorrupt.”
But Dela Rosa’s answer did not carry his signature and was filed through his counsel, Sotto said.
“I received the answer via email on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, 8:51 p.m. It was submitted through his counsel and not signed by him personally,” Sotto said.
“This answer will be considered in the next ethics hearing that will be scheduled at the soonest time,” he added.

In his answer posted on Facebook by his counsel Israelito Torreon, Dela Rosa said he “does not take lightly the duty of a senator to be present, nor the right of any citizen to ask this committee to hold a member to account.”
He said the complaint was only based on “templates, opinion and news” and is only “forcefully worded,” which “establishes no violation of any rule.”

“The Senate’s power to discipline its members is a serious constitutional power and an essential component of legislative independence. It must be exercised with restraint, on clearly defined standards and on concrete evidence,” Dela Rosa said.

The Senate ethics committee is also eyeing amending the Senate rules, which are silent on punishing absences. Dela Rosa has missed his Senate duties since November 2025, until he briefly surfaced last May 11 to help elect his ally Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano as a short-lived Senate president.
